# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 44 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 44 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_044_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 1 — Against Evil Desire

**44:1** He said to me: "Put away from yourself every evil desire and clothe yourself with the desire that is good and holy. For when you clothe yourself with this desire, you shall hate the evil desire and shall bridle it as you will. For the evil desire is fierce and is tamed with difficulty. For it is terrible and greatly consumes men by its fierceness. And most of all, a servant of God is consumed by it if he does not know how to use it."

**44:2** "What then are the works of the evil desire which overthrow the servants of God?" I said. "Tell me, that I may keep away from them." "Listen," he said, "by what works the evil desire slays those who serve God.

**44:3** Above all is the desire for the wife or husband of another, for extravagance in riches, for many needless foods and beverages, and for many other foolish luxuries. For every luxury is foolish and empty for the servants of God. These desires then are evil and produce death for the servants of God. For this evil desire is a daughter of the devil. It is necessary therefore that you keep away from evil desires, so that by keeping away from them you may live to God.

**44:4** But they who are mastered by them and do not resist them shall die utterly, for these desires are to death. But you who follow righteousness and virtue — clothe yourself with the desire for these things, and renouncing every evil desire, put on the desire that is good and noble and acceptable before God, and you shall live to God, every one of you who so lives."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the imperative moral address and the vice-list pattern of Mandate 12.*
